Sudeepti Sharma, J. (Oral)
1.

The present appeal has been preferred against the award dated 21.04.2006 passed in the claim
petition filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 by the learned Motor Accident
Claims Tribunal, Bathinda (for short, 'the Tribunal'), whereby the claim petition filed by the
appellant/claimant for grant of compensation was dismissed.
2.  Learned counsel for the appellant contends that the claim petition is dismissed only on the ground that the name of the driver as well as the number of truck was not mentioned.
3. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3-Insurance Company contends that the claim petition has rightly been dismissed.
4. I have heard the counsel for the parties and perused the whole MOHIT 2024.11.18 10:26

sentences.text: 5. A perusal of the record shows that the truck was parked.
The claimant was accompanied by three more persons, two of whom did not sustain any injury(s).
Therefore, they had an opportunity to promptly note down the registration number of the truck.

Further the assertion that the truck's driver absconded from the place of accident lacks credibility, as the uninjured individuals could reasonably have intervened to prevent the driver's escape from the scene of accident.
6. In view of the above, I do not find any infirmity in the award dated 21.04.2006 passed by learned Tribunal.
Accordingly, the present appeal is dismissed being devoid of any merit.
7. Pending application(s), if any, also stand(s) disposed of.
